svg.title: Designing a day with breathing room

text.tspan: A calendar gives plans a place in time.
Designing a day with breathing room
A meaningful schedule needs more than a full calendar. Protecting valued activities and leaving gaps between
commitments can create the breathing room needed for sustained attention.
First, protecting one priority makes it easier to act on what matters. I made a deliberate adjustment by setting
aside time to read before opening my messages. Some replies had to wait, but reading finally became part of
my day rather than a postponed intention.
Second, small gaps prevent commitments from competing for every available minute. I began leaving a short
break after meetings instead of scheduling another task immediately. That pause helped me recognise when I
was spreading myself too thin and adjust the rest of the day.
Protected priorities and deliberate gaps both make attention more sustainable. Neither requires a completely
empty calendar; each requires accepting limits. I now judge my schedule by the room it gives meaningful
activities, as well as the tasks it contains.
BUILD YOUR OWN · Thesis: attention needs protected priorities and gaps. Explain each with a practical example. Conclude
by acknowledging the trade-off. Follow the main idea through two supported points. The conclusion brings both points
together without adding a new reason.
What two changes does the writer recommend, and what trade-off is involved?
